To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the product of the HAL2 yeast gene is a metabolic enzyme, a phosphatase that catalyses the hydrolysing of 3'-PAP into AMP.

(1) the structure of Hal2, a major salt-sensitive enzyme in yeast, was solved in complex with its substrates and cations and the structure of a salt-insensitive mutant of Hal2 was also solved; (2) two framework interactions were identified in Hal2 which are critical to determine the salt sensitivity of the enzyme; and (3) these interactions are conserved in other salt-sensitive enzymes of the superfamily.

(i) Hal2p is an in vivo sodium and lithium target and its overexpression confers salt tolerance to yeast and plants; (ii) the product of the HAL2 yeast gene is a metabolic PAP phosphatase and the prototype of a large family of PAP-specific enzymes which include inositol monosphatase; (iii) the X-ray structure of yeast PAP phosphatse Hal2p in the presence of magnesium, lithium and products of PAP cleavage
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a salt-tolerant yeast strain and the identification of the structural determinants of salt sensitivity in a family of enzymes.

the structural basis of the cation sensitivity of Hal2p and its relatives, the identification of framework interactions that determine cation sensitivity and the generation of mutants with reduced cation-sensitivity.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the cation sensitivity of Hal2p and its relatives, and the engineering of salt-insensitive enzymes for crop improvement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal structures of Hal2p and inositol monphosphatase are similar, and that the structural basis for cation sensitivity is conserved in these two enzymes.
the structure of Hal2P has revealed the mechanism of cation inhibition and has identified the residues that are critical for the cation sensitivity of the enzyme.
the structure of Hal2 provides a basis for understanding the molecular basis of cation sensitivity and the design of cation insensitive enzymes of this family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structural and functional analysis of Hal2p provides a basis for the rational engineering of cation insensitive PAP phosphatase enzymes and for the identification of new drug targets in the lithium-sensitive inositol monphosphatase superfamily.
the crystal structure of the yeast phosphatase Hal2p, which is a prototype for a large family of enzymes, has provided the structural basis for understanding cation sensitivity in these enzymes.

1) we solved the crystal structure for Hal2p, 2) we identified the residues involved in cation sensitivity and 3) we demonstrated that the same residues are involved in cation binding for Hal2p and inositol monophasphatase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the engineering of salt-tolerants forms of Hal2p or related PAP phosphatase may contribute to the development of salt-toleran plants.
the engineering of cation sensitivity in Hal2p may be achieved through the disruption of framework interactions.
the cation sensitivity of phosphatases can be modulated by mutations of framework interactions.
